## 1. What was read

**952 research articles** from 33 of the 33 journals on the roster, filtered to `journal article` and excluding reviews, editorials, news, comment and case reports.

| General | Cancer | Immune | Bioinfo | Sysbio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 358 | 165 | 81 | 328 | 20 |

!!! warning "Volume swing against the median month: general -26%"
    Check the source before reading anything into this. Two benign causes account for most of these. `bioinfo` every January carries the Nucleic Acids Research database issue and runs high. And several journals simply deposit nothing in some months — queried directly, PubMed returns zero *Nucleic Acids Research* research articles dated 2025-12, and zero *Bioinformatics* in 2024-04, 2025-01, 2025-04 and 2026-03. Those holes are in the source and are reproduced exactly by re-running the harvest, so a swing here is not evidence that a field went quiet and is not usually evidence that the pipeline broke either.

Largest contributors: Nucleic Acids Res 162, Nature 99, Science 80, Bioinformatics 62, J Immunother Cancer 50, JAMA 42.

## 3. The evidence that moved it

**A spatial unit, not a cell type, is what immunotherapy requires.**
[38906155](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38906155/) (*Cancer Cell*): intratumoral immune **triads** are required for
immunotherapy-mediated elimination of solid tumours. The operative requirement is
a multicellular arrangement. Read against the whole
`suppressive-population-inversion` thread, this is the constructive version of
the same objection: if the functional unit is a triad, then depleting or blocking
any single population in it has an unpredictable sign, which is exactly what the
inversion cards keep reporting.

**[38533987](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38533987/) (*Cancer Discov*): paradoxical activation of oncogenic
signalling as a treatment strategy.** The sign of an intervention is treated as
an open question in a review-of-record venue — a year before the corpus starts
logging sign reversals as a pattern.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

[38969522](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38969522/) (*JITC*): infliximab in steroid-refractory immune-related
hepatitis does not demonstrate hepatotoxicity and may shorten time on steroids —
a feared toxicity that does not appear.

### (b) Method credibility

Three concern-and-retraction notices in one month, two of them in the same
journal: [38946327](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38946327/) and [38946326](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38946326/) (*Cancer Discov*, Expressions of
Concern on drug-addiction-based selection against MAPKi-resistant melanoma and
on durable suppression of acquired MEK-inhibitor resistance), and [38870944](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38870944/)
(*Cell*, retraction of a genomic decoding of neuronal depolarisation). Both
*Cancer Discovery* notices attach to resistance-mechanism papers, which is the
literature the `immunotherapy-resistance` thread draws on.

[39030569](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39030569/) (*Genome Biol*) benchmarks methods for correcting biases of
established **and unknown** origin in CRISPR-Cas9 screening data — the unknown
half is the admission. [38951922](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38951922/) evaluates variant-effect predictors by
their ability to infer human traits rather than against curated labels, which is
the same move as the 2026 sequence-to-function evaluations against real
inter-individual variation.
